About

Human System Integration Engineer

I am a Ph.D. student at Texas A&M University, working in the SEAK Lab under Prof. Daniel Selva. My research focuses on autonomous anomaly resolution for space habitats — building physics-based digital twins that can diagnose failures without ground support during deep-space missions.

My path into Human-Systems Integration began with Space Music Hall — my bachelor's capstone project, where I first combined systems engineering with anthropometric design and ECLSS to create a cultural facility module for LEO. That question — "what does human presence in space actually require?" — continues to drive my research.

Previously, I worked as Structural Design Lead at ArkEdge Space and Thermal Operations Engineer at ISAS/JAXA, contributing to missions including EQUULEUS (NASA SLS, 2022), SPHERE EYE-1, and ONGLAISAT.
